title: Commercial Elevation Journey Map — Dedicated & Private (draft)
content:
Status: working draft — for CS team review and playtesting

Purpose:
- Provide a compact, repeatable journey map for upselling production customers from hosted to Dedicated, or from Dedicated to Private (VPC / on-prem), and for adding premium SLA tiers.
- Surface technical gating questions, commercial levers, timing windows (relative to renewal), and reusable QBR / outreach collateral.

Audience:
- Customer Success Managers (CSM) and Solutions Engineers (SE) working mid-market and enterprise accounts with predictable token usage patterns and regulatory concerns.

Success criteria (example):
- 20% of targeted expansion cohort converts to Dedicated trial within 90 days of play kickoff.
- 60% of Private evaluation engagements produce a security/architecture signoff within 120 days.
- Incremental ARR per win > $40k annually.

Triggers to start the journey (prioritization signals):
- Sustained 30% month-over-month (MoM) growth of token consumption above free/hosted thresholds.
- Customer support tickets requesting throughput SLAs, IP isolation, or inbound security reviews.
- Executive requests for vendor security questionnaires (e.g., SOC2, ISO) or procurement mention of on-prem.
- Renewal approaching in 90–180 days with annualized spend in target band.

Stage 0 — Discovery (first contact, 0–14 days):
- Owner: CSM + SE (joint).
- Goals: validate business driver, identify decision-makers, capture technical constraints and procurement cycle.
- Questions: what is current QPS/TPM, average seq length, P95 latency target, data sensitivity classification, regulatory constraints?
- Artifacts to collect: simple spreadsheet (usage profile), architecture diagram, current invoice / pricing band.

Stage 1 — Hypothesis & Value Framing (14–30 days):
- Build an expected unit-economics comparison: hosted per-token vs estimated Dedicated reserved pricing (commits) vs Private licensing. Include projected cost delta at current and 50% growth scenarios.
- Run a short latency/cost sketch: how batching, KV cache, and quantization can reduce per-token cost in Dedicated.
- Deliverable: 1‑pager ROI snapshot + recommended next-step (trial or architecture review).

Stage 2 — Technical Validation Pilot (30–75 days):
- Offer: Dedicated pilot (4–8 weeks) with scoped throughput and representative prompt set OR Private sandbox engagement (security review + isolation PoC).
- SE tasks: baseline perf benchmarks, baseline accuracy/quality check, KV/prefix caching plan, integration plan for metrics/tracing.
- Success criteria: meet latency and throughput targets, no highest-severity security blockers, customer able to run 1–2 production flows end-to-end.

Stage 3 — Commercial Negotiation & Packaging (60–120 days):
- Pricing levers: committed throughput (reserved vCPU/GPU hours), burst credits, support tier (SLA response times), onboarding professional services credits.
- Standard plays: 12-month reserved commitment with quarterly review; 24-month Private license with 6-month phased rollout; premium SLA add-on (4h critical response, financial credits for downtime).
- Objection playbook:
  - "Too expensive": surface unit economics, show cost at scale, propose phased commitment.
  - "Security barriers": route to security & compliance bundle (SaaS + managed private control plane).
  - "Uncertain usage": offer consumption + reserve hybrid structure.

Stage 4 — Close & Onboarding (after contract signature):
- Handoff checklist: SSO/KMS integration, audit logs access, observability dashboards pre-provisioned, runbook for incident triage, scheduled training sessions.
- Time-to-value metric: production traffic within X weeks (goal 4–8).

Renewal & Expansion Timeline (template to track per account):
- Day 0: Play kickoff (capture triggers and baseline).
- Day 30: ROI snapshot sent to exec sponsor.
- Day 60: Pilot metrics review.
- Day 90: Commercial terms proposed.
- Day 120: Contract signed / onboarding scheduled.
- Ongoing: QBR cadence quarterly; expansion opportunities reviewed at each QBR.

Embedded QBR slide checklist (for CSM):
- Title slide: Account, owners, ARR impact of proposed elevation.
- Usage trends: tokens, throughput, latencies, error rates.
- Value realization: cost compare, latency percentiles pre/post pilot.
- Risk signals: integration blockers, backlog tickets by severity.
- Next steps & ask: required exec signoff, procurement timeline, SE deliverables.

Renewal tracker (mini-table that CSM can paste into tracker sheet):
- Account | Renewal date | Current product | Proposed upgrade | Decision maker | Next milestone | Risk level
- (example row) Acme Corp | 2025-06-15 | Hosted | Dedicated (8x GPU pool) + SLA | VP Eng | Pilot complete 2025-02-28 | Medium

Technical gating checklist (SE-friendly):
- Network: can we open necessary egress/ingress? VPC peering or VPN requirements documented?
- Data: PII / regulated workload classification confirmed? KMS & encryption at rest keys agreed?
- Performance: sample prompt set run with <target P95 latency? Are sequence lengths similar to prod?
- Observability: traces, per-route token cost, and tracing hooks verified.

Email/snippet templates (short):
- Exec outreach: "We’ve identified an opportunity to materially reduce model cost and stabilize latency at scale — can we schedule a 20-min ROI review next week?"
- Renewal nudge: "Renewal window approaching — attached recommended Dedicated package based on your usage pattern; happy to walk through numbers."

Escalation flow (if stalled):
- 2 weeks no response after proposal -> SE-led technical drop-in + schedule options.
- 4 weeks no progress -> AE + CSM executive intro; propose fixed-scope pilot at reduced rate.
- Security/legal stalls -> route to security-slots weekly office hours + checklist handoff to legal.

Open questions / things to test in pilot program:
- Minimum pilot duration that reliably surfaces perf regressions? (4 weeks vs 8).
- Which quantization profile gives best cost/quality tradeoff for 70/30 classification/generation mixes?
- Template for measurable SLA credits that procurement accepts without excessive legal review.

Next steps for this doc:
- SEs: add checklist items from recent Private PoC (Marco).
- CSMs: trial this journey on 3 mid-market accounts and capture outcomes (Sara).
- Legal: draft a short SLA addendum template we can attach to proposals (Danielle).

Notes (informal):
- Keep messaging engineer-first. Avoid vendor-lock messaging: focus on predictability, observability, and cost transparency.
- This doc should be paired with a 1-page ROI slide that CSMs can drop in QBR decks.
- Need a small spreadsheet generator that takes account usage + desired margin and outputs recommended commit size (ask product ops).

Revision history: initial draft 2024-11-18 by Priya; SE inputs 2024-12-05; pilot wording updated 2025-01-10.
